title: BeeBot state store
description: Validates both records in this store and documents them. Per-field hints live on `description`, so the rule and the explanation sit together. Loaded at startup; a broken or missing schema refuses every write.

work_name.description: Names one piece of work within its `cwd`. Half of the key -- (cwd, work_name) -- so a name only has to be unique in the directory it runs in, not across the store. Also the filename stem, so it may not start with '.', '_' or '-' and may not contain a path separator -- that is what keeps work_state_path structurally inside states/.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC, second resolution, always 'Z'. Fixed width on purpose: lexicographic order is then chronological, so callers can sort and compare rows as plain strings.

index_row.description: One row of states/index.jsonl. Written by code, never directly. This is the recall path: every field here narrows a search, and nothing here needs a work file opened to be useful.

work_name.description: Unique together with `cwd`. That pair is a cross-record invariant this schema cannot express; `validate` enforces it.

work_state_path.description: '<bucket>/<work_name>.json', relative to states/, where the bucket is an injective rendering of `cwd` -- readable prefix plus a digest of the whole path, so two directories can never share one bucket and overwrite each other. Stored rather than derived, even though slug(cwd) would reproduce it: that keeps the slug function swappable, so changing how buckets are named leaves old rows resolvable. Containment is enforced by resolve_in_store, not by this pattern alone.

cwd.description: The real working directory this work runs in, outside this store. Required -- it is half the key, and it is how the next agent in that directory finds this at all. NOT writable after initialize -- the bucket is derived from it, so a mutable cwd would mean moving files.

short_description.description: One line. This is what makes an index worth having -- the other fields narrow by time and place, but choosing the right work item needs content, and without it every search would have to open every work file.

updated.description: When anything last happened here. Strictly monotonic per work item, so it doubles as the token a stale write is refused against. Always the server's value, never a parameter.

completion.description: The one-bit fact recall filters on. Not `current_status`, which is prose.

work_file.description: One <work_name>.json. Written by AGENTS. Content only -- the index row carries identity, location and time.

description.description: What this is, and what done looks like. `completion` has to be judged against something.

prior_actions.description: Short and high-level: what was attempted, and how it turned out. Dead ends matter most; they are what an arriving agent would otherwise rediscover. Rewritten whole on every write, never appended, so staying short is a choice made each time rather than deferred cleanup.

next_steps.description: What to do next. Rewritten whole.

blockers.description: What is stopping progress. Empty is the normal case. Rewritten whole.

artifacts.description: Durable references only; referenced content lives elsewhere.

item.description: Any durable reference -- a path, link, commit, or job ID.

note.description: What it is and why it matters.

final_learnings.description: OPTIONAL, usually written once at the end. Different audience from `prior_actions`: that serves whoever picks THIS work up, this serves whoever hits the same problem on other work, and is what makes closed records worth keeping.
